xCentreBottom.why: With x on d1, o on a1 raises it and x on a1 lowers it in the training rows (+1.31 vs -1.35, much weaker when d1 is not x), but f1 moves it nearly as much the other way and is not read.

oCentreBottom.why: o on d1 gives the largest penalty and x on d1 the smallest, but the d1 state explains only 24% of the part's variance; b1 and the e/f middle squares move it about as much.

bottomRowVsUpper.why: o pieces on the bottom row and x pieces on rows 2-3 each raise it separately in the training rows (4.46 vs 1.68 at equal bottom-row balance), and that additive reading explains 95% of its variance.

upperRowUnits.why: It does penalise x leading on the second row once the bottom row is held fixed (-2.81 vs -1.53), but its largest swings come from rare column-a upper pieces, which no reading covers.

sideUnits.why: The bottom-row line reading appears only on constructed 6-piece boards outside the data; on real positions three x in a row on the bottom row hardly changes it (2.51 vs 2.38).
